research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; higher-risk building control approval, application information, controlled changes and completion-certificate methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Agreed documents and controlled changes
verified_claims: Approved application documents become agreed documents; changes to them are controlled changes.
limitations: A document comparison is needed to establish whether a change occurred.

sources.name: Assessing and recording changes
verified_claims: Each controlled change must be managed under the change-control plan and recorded in the change-control log.
limitations: Recording a change does not prove its regulatory classification is correct.

sources.name: Notifiable change timing
verified_claims: BSR must be told before work involving a notifiable change starts.
limitations: Notification is not the same as approval of a major change.

sources.name: Notifiable-change scope
verified_claims: Potentially compliance-affecting changes to specified plans, unit layouts, penetrations, supports, fire documents or staged-work documents can be notifiable.
limitations: The category depends on the exact technical effect of the change.

sources.name: Replacement-product classification
verified_claims: Same or higher specification replacement can be recordable, while changed reaction-to-fire specification may be notifiable.
limitations: Nominal product labels are insufficient without performance documentation.

sources.name: Work after notifiable submission
verified_claims: After a notifiable change is submitted, related work may proceed unless BSR directs that it should have been a major change.
limitations: Submission does not protect work if the change was misclassified.

sources.name: Major-change approval
verified_claims: Major changes require BSR approval before the change or related building work starts.
limitations: Proposed approval cannot be inferred from submission or validation.

sources.name: Material change of use
verified_claims: A material change of use of part of the proposed building is treated as a major change.
limitations: The legal classification depends on the proposed and existing uses.

sources.name: Late partial-completion strategy
verified_claims: Adding a partial-completion strategy after approval without one requires a major-change application.
limitations: The requirement does not show that a strategy is technically adequate.

sources.name: Major-change examples
verified_claims: Major changes can include alterations to height, storeys, escape routes, external walls, fire measures, common parts, unit numbers or structural design.
limitations: The example list does not replace project-specific assessment.

sources.name: Stopping work for major changes
verified_claims: Work related to a proposed major change must stop until BSR approval is obtained.
limitations: Stopping related work does not necessarily require stopping unrelated work.

sources.name: Submitting changes online
verified_claims: The online service is used for notifiable changes, dutyholder changes and major-change applications.
limitations: Online submission does not prove the required supporting detail is complete.

sources.name: Change application information
verified_claims: Change submissions explain the change, classification, reason, regulatory effects and affected agreed documents.
limitations: A reasoned submission is not evidence of approval.

sources.name: Major-change assessment period
verified_claims: Unless extended, BSR can take up to 6 weeks to assess a major-change application.
limitations: The period is not a guaranteed decision date.

sources.name: Validation and decision outcomes
verified_claims: A complete application can proceed to assessment and may be approved, approved with requirements or rejected.
limitations: Validation does not mean approval, and conditions must be satisfied before affected work begins.
